dialogue.user: Those are some interesting options! I'm particularly drawn to "Ausgrenor: The first novel in the Raising Up Pharaoh series" because of the author's background in archaeology and history. Could you tell me more about the book's plot or genre? Also, is it part of a series, and if so, how many books are in the series?
dialogue.agent:
**"Ausgrenor: The first novel in the Raising Up Pharaoh series"** is indeed an intriguing choice. It's the first novel in a six-book epic series set in the Fertile Crescent at the dawn of written history. The story unfolds through the viewpoints of various characters, including orphans, a couple, and their foes, as they navigate the challenges of their time. The book is written for readers of all ages and maintains an intense tone while avoiding excessive violence and sexuality. The diverse cast speaks a pidgin of proto-Indo-European, proto-Afro-Semitic, and various lost languages, presented in modern U.S. English. The series was edited by Dr. Dennis E. Hensley PhD.

Here is a top review for the book:

**Review:**
*I read all six books of the Raising up Pharaoh series over a period of about two weeks. The story line was so intriguing; I could hardly put them down. I love reading; and history, wars, geography, archaeology, biography, adventure, education, technology, inspiration, miracles, romance, humor and irony are all included in the events and lives of the characters of these books. Patros, the head of the family and most admirable character, was under constant temptation and pressure to make personal and administrative decisions for himself and his people that were not in keeping with his desire to follow the will of his one god, the God of Creation. Many other admirable characters (both Eurasian and Bedouin) were ordinary people who were subjected to the temptations and errors in judgment of all humans but were inspired and thrilled to learn what it meant to have God enter their lives and make them instrumental in his plan. It is easy to identify with these people even today. The most difficult aspect of reading the books for me was keeping track of the many characters and places with unfamiliar but similarly-spelled names. Using the author’s website http://www.raisinguppharaoh.com/ in parallel was helpful in understanding their meanings. But I found the most interesting and helpful tool was studying the maps that are included in the books to keep track of the movement and routes they traveled. Sometimes it was difficult to keep track of the time line of the various events, because the story covered the actions and relationships of a wide variety of characters and locations. However, the overall story was fascinating, educational and entertaining. I recommend and consider this series a “must read” for friends and family.*

result.title: Ausgrenor: The first novel in the Raising Up Pharaoh series
result.features: 5,203 years ago, cruel eastern invaders annihilate villages in the wintry Sakros Mountains. Survivors flood west into the fertile plain between the rivers, seeking refuge among its walled cities. Three shepherd boys see their families executed and flee to one of their caves, where they find eight starving girls and bodies of others. Unwilling to abandon them, the boys hide them in a remote cave in the high forest, and feed and equip them until they’re fit to travel. Weida, widowed princess of an overrun kingdom, joins them on their trek to Ausgrenor. She seeks Patros, widower-brother of her late husband. Fortified cities fall. Ausgrenor stands alone. Terrified citizens regress into savagery. Their vicious king plots to rob the rich and flee. Neighboring Bedu tribes slip away into the desert. Invaders approach. Patros is torn between ancestral loyalties and survival of his new wards. Fight or flee. Now or never. Thus begins the six-novel Raising Up Pharaoh epic, set among the emerging city-states and nations in the Fertile Crescent at the dawn of written history—as they plant the cultural seeds of today’s world. The series is written for readers of all ages. The tone is intense, yet controlled by zooming back the lens to avoid needless close-ups of violence and sexuality. The tale unfolds through the differing viewpoints of the orphans, the couple, others drawn to them, and their foes. This first book’s setting ranges across the southwestern mountains of what is now called Iran, southern Iraq between the lower Tigris and Euphrates rivers, the marshes of their delta with the Persian Gulf, and is bounded on the west by the Saudi Arabian desert. In later books, the setting expands throughout the Middle East, the Steppes, West and South Asia, and Northwest Africa. Each book has its own maps. The diverse cast speaks a pidgin of proto-Indo-European, proto-Afro-Semitic, and various lost languages such as Harappan. The pidgin is presented in modern U.S. English. The Raising Up Pharaoh novels were edited by Dr. Dennis E. Hensley PhD
